messages:
mari: Heads-up — saw a noticeable perf regression on the long-context e2e runs. KV cache memory climbs steadily and p99 tails spike when continuous batching merges lots of small slots together. Repro steps below and a quick flamegraph dump.

mari: Repro command I used:```./tools/perf_run --profile longctx --concurrency 16 --seq 4096 --iters 5000 > run.log```

sanjay: Can you paste the flamegraph or the hot stacks?

mari: Flamegraph shows a big flat hotspot in the slot coordinator split/merge path, and a bunch of time in kv_page_reassemble and kv_fragment_scan. snippet:```slot_coordinator::handle_split 38%
kv_page_reassemble     22%
kv_fragment_scan        14%
encoder::write_kv       8%
other                  18%```

josh: That matches an observation from yesterday — the coordinator is splitting aggressively once slots exceed residency threshold which produces many small merges that block the head of the batch queue. Small merges hold the prefix KV lock longer and cause head-of-line blocking for following batches.

mari: Numbers: baseline p99 on master (no regression) ~240ms. After the change p99 ~620ms. Memory: working set for KV went from ~1.8GB -> ~3.6GB during the run (longctx workloads).

tk: Could kernel selection be a factor? If small-batch code paths fall back to a generic kernel, we might see extra allocs/copies while waiting. I saw a fallback in kernel_select.log:```seq_len>1024 -> used: matmul_ref_kernel (fallback), estimated_tokens=4096```

perf-bot: :warning: Perf alert: test "longctx-heavy" p99 increased by 170% vs baseline. Related tag: kv/slot-coord.

josh: Quick mitigation idea: delay small merges for a short window (e.g., 5-10ms) to allow coalescing of slot fragments and give KV time to evict/compact prefix pages. That should reduce number of split+merge cycles and the HOL blocking.

mari: I tried bumping contbatch.split_threshold from 0.7 -> 0.92 and also landed an experiment branch slot-coord/delay-merge. Ran 100 iters: p99 improved ~30% vs regression (so down from 620ms -> ~430ms) but CPU increased by ~8% and overall mem still higher than baseline (2.9GB).

sanjay: Can you capture eviction and fragmentation counters while the test runs? Need to see if fragmentation spikes right after merges.

mari: Eviction log snippet shows repeated small evict/alloc churn:```[kv] evict_page id=0x7fffa3 size=4096 fragments=3
[kv] alloc_page id=0x7fffa5 size=4096 fragments=0
[kv] fragmented_pages=312 -> 524 -> 738 (during 1k-2k requests)```

josh: The fragmented_pages ramp implies reassembly path is slow. If page chain reassembly is O(n) and we get frequent small splits, reuse is inhibited. We should consider an opportunistic coalescer (buddy-style) that runs incrementally rather than monolithic reassembly in the hot path.

tk: I'll run memguard + kernel selection trace to correlate times where kernel falls back with allocation spikes. If fallback happens on small batch sizes, delayed-merge might increase small-batch count and worsen kernel selection regressions — need to watch that tradeoff.

mari: Steps to reproduce (short):
1) start server: `./bin/redwoodd --cfg profiles/longctx.yaml --kv-size 6G`
2) run: `./tools/perf_run --profile longctx --concurrency 16 --seq 4096 --iters 5000`
3) tail /debug/kv/fragmentation and kernel_select.log
4) capture flame at iteration ~250

infra-bot: New experiment branch created: https://git.internal/r/slot-coord/delay-merge — CI: unit tests passed, perf job queued.

mari: Next actions I propose: A) get a full KV allocator flame (alloc stacks) for the run B) try delayed-merge in a prod-like env with kernel selection logging enabled C) instrument reassembly path to break out per-iteration cost so we can see whether it's linear vs amortized. Anyone object?

josh: :thumbsup:

sanjay: fine with that, ping me when you have traces so I can prototype a lightweight coalescer.

mari: I'll upload the run logs and flame outputs to the perf bucket and ping the thread when ready. Thanks all.
